narr: Clusters of thunderstorms with very high rainfall rates from 2 to 4 inches per hour developed by midday on June 20, and despite being transient, continued to redevelop through the evening and into the overnight hours. The primary focus occurred along Highway 18 in the afternoon southwest and south of Sioux Falls, then along Interstate 90 during the evening, and settled again to along the Highway 18 corridor as the effective cold pool boundary collapsed southward through the night. The final 24 hour rainfall totals reached 6 to 12 inches by daybreak from eastern Hutchinson County eastward through Turner and Lincoln counties.
ev: Heavy rainfall through the early to mid-afternoon, which totaled 3 to 4 inches, yielded runoff which inundated several rural roads with significant flowing water. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lincoln County.

Rainfall from 2 to 4 inches over a three hour period in the early evening led to multiple roads closed due to standing water. One home was damaged by water on south Main St. near Avenue of Flags in Chamberlain. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Brule County.

Early evening rainfall was intense with 2 to 2.5 inches in a couple of hours, which resulted in widespread flash flooding in Plankinton. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Aurora County.

After heavy rainfall earlier in the day, another 5 to 8 inches rainfall between midnight and 3 am CST lead to widespread street flooding in Canton with at least one swift water rescue. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lincoln County.

Highway 81 south of Salem was impassable due to flooding near 257th Street. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for McCook County.

South Dakota Highway 42 was closed due to water flowing over the highway around 1 mile east of the intersection with U.S. Highway 81. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for McCook County.

After as much as 3 to 5 inches of rainfall between 8 pm and 11 pm, flash flooding pushed water up to homes and flooded basements in many portions of the city of Mitchell. No travel was recommended with numerous stranded motorists, and portions of Interstate 90 were closed due to water flowing over the road. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Davison County.

Continued rainfall exacerbated flooding of roads with numerous barricaded and impassable. Several homes had flooded basements. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Aurora County.

After rainfall of up to 3 to 4 inches during a couple hours around midnight, water on city streets in Tea flowed up to 18 inches deep in some locations. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lincoln County.

After an estimated 3 to 4 inches of rain since late morning, increasing runoff resulted in water flowing over 443rd Street 2 miles north of U.S. Highway 18. Numerous gravel roads were also inundated by water. Four swift water rescues were performed. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Turner County.

Heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches over a couple hours led to a breach at Healy Dam, where a home was also damaged by flowing water. Panzour and Sharpings Lake Dam were also breached due to excessive runoff. Numerous county roads were inundated by standing and flowing water. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Brule County.

As a result of late evening rainfall from 3 to 5 inches in a couple hours, the city of Spencer lift stations could not keep up with water levels. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for McCook County.

Rainfall from 2 to 4 inches in a couple of hours late evening caused significant street flooding in Salem, along with several homes with flooded basements. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for McCook County.

Rainfall between 3 and 5 inches between 11 pm and 2 am resulted in significant flooding of portions of Interstate 29 near mile marker 69. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Lincoln County.

After 3 to 4 inches of rainfall between 11 pm and 2 am, the river levels at Split Rock Creek near Corson gage site COSS2 reached flood stage at 2 am CDT. For a more comprehensive description of flood damage, please see other entries for areal and river flooding for Minnehaha County.
